2026-12-07.title: Monday of the Second Week of Advent · St Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor
readings: Here is your God; he will come and save you
Our God will come to save us!
Friend, your sins are forgiven you
2026-12-07.alt: Memorial of St Ambrose, bishop and doctor of the Church.
2026-12-07.verse: When he saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you.”
theo: Isaiah 35 is a song of the desert in bloom: “The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad… Strengthen the weak hands… Say to those who are of a fearful heart, ‘Be strong, do not fear! Here is your God… He will come and save you.’” Then the eyes of the blind are opened, the lame leap like a deer, and the redeemed walk the Holy Way home with singing.

In the Gospel the prophecy walks into a crowded house. Friends cannot get their paralysed companion near Jesus, so they open the roof and lower him down. “When he saw their faith”, Jesus first forgives his sins, then, to show that “the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”, tells him to stand up and walk. The deepest healing is forgiveness; the first miracle Advent asks for is a good Confession. St Ambrose, bishop of Milan, preached this mercy and baptised St Augustine at Easter 387.
outline: Ask: whom are you carrying to Jesus in prayer?
Friends carry the paralysed man to Jesus.
“Here is your God; he will come and save you.”
live: Bring a friend's need to Jesus in prayer every day this week.
2026-12-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of the friends and forgave the paralysed man. Strengthen my weak hands, make the dry places of my life bloom, and give me the joy of your forgiveness. Amen.
altar: At Mass we bring before the Lord all those we carry in our hearts. The One who said, your sins are forgiven, gives himself to us as food for the journey.

quick: Friends' faith brings the paralysed man to Jesus.
2026-12-07.action: Pray daily for a friend who needs Jesus.
2026-12-07.question: Whom am I carrying to Jesus?

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. Jesus forgave his sins and healed him. We can bring our friends to Jesus by praying for them.
family.intention: We pray for a friend or relative who needs Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we ‘carry’ to Jesus in our prayer this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of those who carried their friend. As we gather, we bring to you all those we love who cannot come by themselves. Amen.
share: Jesus saw their faith (Luke 5:20). Whose faith has carried me to Jesus?
Whom am I carrying in prayer, and have I given up too soon?
Isaiah says: be strong, do not fear (Isaiah 35:4). What fear do I need to hand over?
interc: For the Church, that she may carry the weak and the paralysed to Christ.
For bishops, that like St Ambrose they may lead many to Christ.
For the sick and disabled, that they may find healing and dignity.
For those far from the faith, that our prayer may carry them home.
For all who are afraid, that they may hear: here is your God.
pm.close: Lord God, through St Ambrose you led Augustine to faith. Strengthen our weak hands and feeble knees, and make us faithful in carrying others to your Son. Amen.

illus: For twelve years a mother in Thalassery prayed every day for her son who had left the Church. Her prayer group prayed with her. One Christmas he came home and went to confession. She said: “We were the four men on the roof.”

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah paints a picture of joy: the wilderness and the dry land shall be glad, the desert shall rejoice and blossom. Strengthen the weak hands, make firm the feeble knees. Say to those who are of a fearful heart: be strong, do not fear! Here is your God (Isaiah 35:1–4).
He promises that the eyes of the blind will be opened, the lame will leap like a deer and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy (Isaiah 35:5–6). These are the signs of the Messiah.

In the Gospel some men bring a paralysed man on a bed to Jesus. The crowd is too great, so they go up on the roof and let him down through the tiles right in front of Jesus. When he saw their faith, he said: friend, your sins are forgiven you (Luke 5:18–20).

Notice: their faith. The paralysed man could not come by himself. His friends carried him, and they did not give up when the door was blocked. Jesus saw their faith and healed their friend. We can carry others to Jesus by our prayer and our love.
Notice too that Jesus first forgives sins, then heals the body. The deepest paralysis is sin. Then he says: stand up, take your bed and go home. And the man went home glorifying God (Luke 5:24–25).

Today we remember St Ambrose, bishop of Milan, who carried many to Christ, among them the young Augustine. Let us think of someone who cannot come to Jesus alone: a relative far from the faith, a sick friend, a struggling neighbour. Let us carry them in prayer this Advent, and not give up when the door seems blocked. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends carried a sick man to Jesus. You can carry your friends to Jesus by praying for them!

intro: God makes the desert bloom, friends carry the paralysed man, Christ forgives.

q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say to those who are of a fearful heart, “Be strong, do not fear! Here is your God. He will come with vengeance, with terrible recompense. He will come and save you.”
Amazement seized all of them, and they glorified God and were filled with awe, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”

sub: The friends would not give up.
q: Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
When he saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you.”
points.apply: Pray daily for a friend in need.

sub: Christ gives this authority to his Church.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the Pit, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy.
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—he said to the one who was paralyzed—“I say to you, stand up and take your bed and go to your home.”

concl: Let him forgive and raise you up.
2026-12-07.resolve: Bring someone with you to the parish Advent Confession service.
